bib.title: L-Eval: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Long Context Language Models

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed only; appendix examples B.1-B.20 read.

question: How can long-context LLMs be evaluated in a standardized way, with high-quality diverse datasets and metrics that agree with human judgment?
hypothesis: N-gram metrics do not correlate with human judgment for long-context open-ended generation; length-instruction-enhanced evaluation and LLM judges correlate better.
contributions: A suite of 20 sub-tasks, 508 long documents and 2,000+ human-labeled query-response pairs (3k-200k tokens)
A study of metric correlation with human judgment, proposing Length-Instruction-Enhanced (LIE) evaluation and LLM judges
Evaluation of 4 commercial and 12 open-source LCLMs, with findings on retrieval vs full context and NTK scaling

method.summary: Built L-Eval from 4 scratch-annotated, 4-5 re-annotated and ~12 manually cleaned datasets, split into closed-ended (exam accuracy) and open-ended tasks (human, LLM pairwise judge vs Turbo-16k-0613, n-gram). Validated metrics against 3 human annotators on an 85-question subset, then benchmarked 16 LCLMs, with and without retrieval.

datasets.name: L-Eval (20 sub-tasks)
datasets.size: 508 long documents, 2,000+ query-response pairs; avg input 4k-60k tokens, max ~200k (Llama2 tokenizer)
datasets.source: TOEFL, GSM8k, QuALITY, Coursera, TopicRet, SFiction, CodeU, MultiDoc2Dial, Qasper, LongFQA, NQ, CUAD, NarrativeQA, Multi-News, GovReport, BigPatent, SummScreen, Openreview, QMSum, SPACE; licences not stated
datasets.preprocessing: All samples manually filtered/corrected; Claude-100k used to flag mistaken or unanswerable QAs (answer mismatch -> re-annotate or remove)

inference.decoding: greedy search in the human-evaluation study (to minimize variance); not stated elsewhere
inference.samples: one output per item per model; human study: two runs (with and without length instruction)
inference.prompting: zero-shot with task templates in App B; length instruction appends 'Answer this question with xx words' where xx is reference length; GSM 16-shot CoT; document input truncated from the right
inference.retrieval: OpenAI AdaEmbedding (dense) and BM25 (sparse); top 4 chunks of 1k tokens given to Turbo-4k-0613

parameters.judge pairs: order swapped to reduce positional bias; GPT-4 96x2 rounds, GPT-3.5 181x2 rounds

other.hardware: single NVIDIA A800 GPU with FlashAttention
other.judge prompt addition: Additional details or information that are not mentioned in the reference answer cannot be considered as advantages and do not let them sway your judgment.

metrics.name: Exam accuracy
metrics.definition: exact match; each question scores 100/number of questions; Coursera multi-answer gets a quarter of points if not all correct options chosen; SFiction averages loyalty and factuality

metrics.name: Win-rate vs Turbo-16k-0613
metrics.definition: pairwise battle judged by GPT-4 or GPT-3.5, reference answer given; ties reported

metrics.name: Kendall-Tau
metrics.definition: rank correlation between metric and average human score over 7 models

eval.protocol: Metric validation: 85-question subset, 7 models, 3 annotators, Kendall-Tau; no seeds or significance tests reported.

prompts.text: [Origin Instruction]: Please summarize the opinions of the professor. [Length Instruction]: We need a 50-word summary, where 50 is the number of words in the reference answer
Additional details or information that are not mentioned in the reference answer cannot be considered as advantages and do not let them sway your judgment.
Answer this question with xx words.

results.claim: Adding the reference word count to the instruction (LIE) raises ROUGE-L Kendall-tau with human scores from 0.5 to 0.8; GPT-4 judge reaches 1.
results.setup: 85-question subset, 7 models, 3 human annotators, Kendall-Tau vs average human score (Fig 2)
results.quote: τ has been improved from 0.5 to 0.8 for ROUGE-L

results.claim: Without length control, Claude-100k scores very low F-1 on NQ because its outputs are far too long; with LIE it reaches 57.76.
results.setup: NQ, Claude-100k, F-1 against reference, Delta L 135 words vs 1 with LIE
results.quote: For instance, Claude-100k only achieves a 9.84 F-1
results.table: Table 2, rows Claude-100k and + Length Instruction, NQ F-1 (9.84 -> 57.76)

results.claim: GPT-4-32k is best on closed-ended tasks, average 73.11 vs Claude-100k 65.97 and Turbo-16k 60.73.
results.setup: L-Eval closed-ended exam accuracy, six tasks averaged

results.claim: Claude-100k has the highest win-rate against Turbo-16k-0613 on open-ended tasks under a GPT-4 judge.
results.setup: 96-question subset, GPT-4 judge, pairwise with swapped order (96x2 rounds), vs Turbo-16k-0613
results.table: Table 4, row Claude1.3-100k, column GPT-4 win-rate %

results.claim: Best open-source 16k model wins only 34% against Turbo-16k under the GPT-4 judge, 8 points below its short-context counterpart.
Retrieval over 4k Turbo lags full 16k context on closed-ended tasks (AdaEmb 49.73 vs 60.73 avg), largely because GSM (16-shot) and CodeU cannot be solved by retrieval.

results.claim: CodeU is the hardest task; best model GPT-4-32k gets 25.55%.

results.claim: Benchmark size: 20 sub-tasks, 508 long documents, 2,000+ human-labeled query-response pairs, input length 3k-200k tokens.
Open-source long-context models produce many Level-1 (unhelpful) outputs on long inputs, e.g. Vicuna-7b-16k 138 Level-1 outputs vs Claude-100k 27 without length instruction.
results.table: Table 5, Original evaluation results, row Vicuan-7b-16k, column #Level-1

limits: LLM judge cannot see the full long input, so it relies on the reference answer and question; length bias is more pronounced.
GPT-4 judging all 1000+ open-ended questions is unaffordable; judge results cover only a 96-question subset, human results only 85 questions.
Human study uses 3 annotators who are PhD students working on LCLMs; 7 models, so Kendall-Tau over few items.
Judge prompt text is only partly given; decoding settings for non-human-study runs are not stated.
Models and API snapshots (Claude 1.3, GPT-4-32k, Llama2 era) have dated.
Dynamic NTK rule found not to hold in practice; analysis limited to Coursera truncation.
